extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers of Popular Science Monthly and related professionals (librarians, educators, architects, naturalists, legal scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria used by a 19th-century Popular Science Monthly reviewer to judge books, atlases, library projects, schoolbooks, architectural theory, and natural-history monographs; includes operational and pedagogical standards for libraries and schoolbooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free circulating library accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Books to be lent out free of expense to anybody and everybody who wished them, the only requirement being that some reference should be given to satisfy the librarian that the borrower had a fixed residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove every possible impediment to the procurement of books; begin experimentally and scale up if demand meets supply; locate branches so they are readily accessible to the population; consider opening on Sunday (the only leisure day of working classes) to reach laboring people; attach reading-rooms to each circulating library so patrons receive more attention from librarians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book selection with reference to community wants
rubrics_metrics.description: The books are to be selected with special reference to the wants of each community, carefully excluding all works of doubtful influence for good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select with regard to the needs of the local constituency (especially poorer districts); prioritize wholesome intellectual food for young persons (ages 14–21); use bulletins (lists of works or articles) to suggest reading and direct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library performance and usage metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure library success by volumes circulated, circulation per volume, number of readers, demographic reached, percentage of fiction in circulation, and loss rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example metrics from the report: library contained 5,085 volumes; assumed 4,000 available books circulated 71,750 times ≈ each volume circulated over seventeen times; total readers 9,605; sixty-four percent of circulation was fiction (noted as a comparatively small percentage); only six volumes lost during the year. Compare returns with other libraries to judge relative success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and organizational strategy for public libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish small libraries located in the centers of the poorest and most thickly-settled districts of the city, with reading-rooms attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small scale allows more librarian attention; aim to make libraries 'readily accessible to all the population'; solicit generous support from wealthy citizens to carry out plans promptly and effectively; public endorsement (e.g., mayoral and civic speakers) can strengthen appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schoolbook pedagogical principle: active inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'First-Book' treating of objects that does not provide, first of all, for the active effort of inquiry on the part of the pupil — so that he shall find out the properties of objects for himself — fails of its purpose as a means of education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when facts are selected judiciously, a school book must promote active investigation rather than 'pouring the facts into the little mental pitchers'; teachers should bring objects into the classroom for inspection and add questions; mere concise trustworthy presentation is not enough for sound pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific atlas/map standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Stellar atlases and catalogues should keep accurately to established standards (e.g., Argelander's) and provide accurate positions and brightnesses down to a stated magnitude within the required region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full description of methods of observation, tabulated catalogue, and an atlas that 'gives an exact pictorial representation of the state of the sky at the epoch of the work'; include detailed shadings and gradations of the Milky Way derived from repeated observations and revisions; produce high artistic and mechanical finish; make works available (e.g., bilingual catalogue) for observatories and libraries despite production difficulties and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical and analytical value in legal scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal treatise should be analytical and practical — addressing principles and attempting to place legal doctrine on sound (even scientific) footing — and be useful to the students and practitioners of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupy new ground by connecting law to natural conditions of society; aim for usefulness to students rather than mere formal erudition; covering a comprehensive range of subjects in clear chapters is a virtue even if the work lacks notes or citation apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel writing standard: life-like, informative, and research-oriented
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel and adventure accounts should be life-like and give information about geography, people, governments, customs, and antiquities, and when possible contribute original archaeological or antiquarian research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added material that sheds light on antiquities or previously little-known subjects (e.g., Cambodian ruins) increases value; travel works that prompt further scientific attention and more exact explorations are particularly desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural-history monograph criterion: factual observation and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural-history monographs should faithfully relate and illustrate the facts observed about species' habits, nests, range, and ecology, leaving broad inferences to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide thorough observational detail (distribution, nest architecture, caste differences, food sources), include illustrations/plates, document geographic range, and make a clearly factual contribution (especially valuable when a first or early account of a species or group).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear definition and causal categorization in social/medical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies on social-medical topics (e.g., suicide) should start with clear definitions and classify causes into coherent categories (external/social vs internal/personal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the phenomenon precisely (e.g., 'intentional destruction of one's own life' excluding unintended acts); analyze causes as general external, special external (social relations), and internal/personal (ill health, insanity, temperament); base prevention proposals on legal measures, religious/moral training, and medical advice/treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture: expression of ideas by structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The province of architecture is to express ideas by structures — buildings should give expression to the acts performed within their walls and embody the idea in form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating architecture as only creating pleasant monuments; prioritize structural integrity and purpose over show; produce forms and decorative elements that correspond to and express the function and social import of the building's uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture: technical training and principled practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Good architecture depends on study and acquaintance with technical principles rather than relying on taste or common sense alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training and technical knowledge are essential; resist dilettanteism and 'false taste'; architects should be conscientious, avoid unmeaning display, and not sacrifice expressive clarity for economical mechanical expedients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organic relation between ornament and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek an organic relation between the ornament and the structure — ornamentation should arise from and correspond to the organism of the monument itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the structure forms that correspond with the groups performing acts inside, and use masses, modeling, carved and color decoration to express appropriate degrees of stability, dignity, and elegance.

rubrics_metrics.name: High production and revision standards for scientific/large works
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarly works requiring large-scale production (atlases, catalogues) should undergo repeated observation, revisions, and careful proof correction even when printing logistics are difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The production process (proofs requiring multiple corrections, long-distance printing and delays) affects the final quality; perseverance in repeated corrections and attention to mechanical and artistic finish are credited as part of the work's scientific faithfulness and usefulness.
